stem: A risk ratio (relative risk) compares what between two groups?

options.label: A
options.text: Odds of prior exposure among cases versus among controls
options.misconception: Confuses the risk ratio with the odds ratio from a case-control study.
options.explanation: Comparing the odds of prior exposure in cases and controls gives the odds ratio, the measure of association used in case-control studies.

options.label: B
options.text: Risk of the health event within a single group
options.misconception: Confuses a single group's risk (incidence proportion) with a ratio comparing two groups.
options.explanation: The risk of an event within a single group is an incidence proportion; a risk ratio needs a second group's risk to compare against.

options.label: C
options.text: Baseline characteristics of participants in the two groups
options.misconception: Confuses a measure of association with a check of baseline comparability.
options.explanation: Baseline characteristics are compared to check that groups are similar at the start; this describes the groups, not their risk of an outcome.

options.label: D
options.text: Risk of death among people who already have the disease
options.misconception: Confuses a comparison of groups with case-fatality risk among those with the disease.
options.explanation: The risk of death among people who already have a disease is the case-fatality rate, a single-group measure of severity, not a comparison.

options.label: E
options.text: Risk of a health event in one group versus another
options.misconception: None — the risk ratio compares the risk of a health event between two groups.
options.explanation: CDC: a risk ratio, also called relative risk, compares the risk of a health event among one group with the risk among another group.

context: Learning objective: A risk ratio (relative risk) compares the risk of a health event in one group with the risk in another group.
imageCaption: CDC risk ratio, odds ratio, and attributable proportion.
